items.name: University of Latvia
items.desc: The country’s leading comprehensive university, with broad strengths in the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences and law.

items.name: Riga Technical University
items.desc: A principal centre for engineering, information technology, architecture and applied sciences, with a strong international profile.

items.name: Rīga Stradiņš University
items.desc: Internationally recognised for English-taught medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, nursing and health sciences programmes.

items.name: Latvia University of Life Sciences and Technologies
items.desc: Specialising in agriculture, veterinary medicine, food technology, forestry, environmental sciences and engineering.

items.name: BA School of Business and Finance
items.desc: A business-focused institution offering English-taught programmes in management, finance, cybersecurity and entrepreneurship.

items.name: Stockholm School of Economics in Riga
items.desc: An internationally oriented premier business school offering respected Bachelor’s and executive education in economics and management.

items.name: RISEBA University of Applied Sciences
items.desc: Combines business, creative industries, architecture, audiovisual media and information technology with a practice-oriented approach.

items.name: Turiba University
items.desc: Focused on business administration, tourism, hospitality management, law and communication, with close links to industry.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.intro: Common questions about studying and settling in Latvia.

items.q: Can I study in Latvia entirely in English?
items.a: Yes. Latvian universities offer a wide choice of English-taught programmes at Bachelor’s, Master’s and doctoral level, including medicine, dentistry, engineering, business and information technology.

items.q: Do I need to speak Latvian?
items.a: It is not required for English-taught programmes, though learning basic Latvian or Russian is helpful for daily life and part-time work. Universities typically offer introductory language courses.

items.q: How much does it cost to study in Latvia?
items.a: Latvia is one of Europe’s most affordable study destinations. Tuition for non-medical programmes is commonly in the range of €2,500 to €6,000 per year, while medicine and dentistry cost €10,000 to €15,000. Monthly living costs typically range from €450 to €700.

items.q: When are the intakes and deadlines?
items.a: The main intake begins in September, with a smaller intake in February at some institutions. Medicine and health programmes often close applications earlier in the year (April–June), so early application is advisable.

items.q: Do I need to take an entrance examination?
items.a: Many programmes assess applicants on academic record and a motivation letter. Medicine and health programmes usually require evidence of biology and chemistry preparation and an online entrance test or interview.
Universities usually accept IELTS (5.5–6.5), TOEFL or an equivalent, and some conduct their own interview or test.

items.q: How much money must I show for the visa and residence permit?
items.a: Applicants must demonstrate sufficient funds for their stay. In practice, proof of around €3,000 to €5,000 for the first year is commonly expected, often alongside payment of the first tuition instalment.

items.q: Can I work while studying in Latvia?
items.a: Non-EU students holding a residence permit for study may generally work up to 20 hours per week during term and full-time during official summer holidays.

items.q: Can I remain in Latvia after graduating?
items.a: Graduates may apply for a temporary residence permit to seek employment or start a business, and may then transition to a long-term work-based permit.

items.q: Are scholarships available for international students?
items.a: Yes. Options include Latvian State scholarships under bilateral agreements, Erasmus+ opportunities and merit-based tuition fee reductions from individual universities.
Students may choose university residences (€100–€200/month), which are usually the most economical option, or private rental apartments in Riga (€250–€450/month).

Typically: passport, academic transcripts and certificates (with apostille/AIC recognition), language-test results, CV, motivation letter, proof of financial means, proof of accommodation and health insurance.

items.q: How does EUROPA FUSION support my application?
items.a: We assist at every stage: profile assessment, university selection, AIC document verification, application prep, entrance coaching, visa support, accommodation and pre-departure briefing.
